Why Midland businesses miss calls

Midland is the business hub of the Permian Basin, one of the country’s largest oil-producing regions. Its median household income, about $90,000, is well above other West Texas cities. Oilfield services, equipment repair and trucking run long hours in remote places where cell coverage can be weak. Crews and owners can be out of reach for much of the day, so calls need someone or something to catch them.

Which Midland businesses benefit most?

  • HVAC and contractors: West Texas heat and a busy housing market keep crews booked.
  • Auto and truck repair: Work trucks that stop earn nothing, so drivers need fast answers.
  • Real estate agents: Workers relocating to the basin call from out of town.

What a call could sound like in Midland

Here is an example of how a call might go. Your script, rules and wording would be set up with you.

Caller: Our service truck is down on the south side. Can you get to it today?

AI receptionist: Gets the location and problem, flags it urgent and sends it to your on-call number.

Does your Midland AI receptionist need Spanish?

About 28.3% of Midland residents age 5 and older speak Spanish at home. Nearly three in ten residents speak Spanish at home. A bilingual agent suits field crews, home services and medical offices. Our AI calling agents and AI receptionists speak English and Spanish, and you can read more on our bilingual AI calling agent page.

Can you keep your Midland phone number?

Yes. Midland callers will usually see the 432 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
